# q36 f=2, 2K1 far, a_F=1 — exact q35 shell generated by a multiplicity-three one-edge support

Status: `PROVED REDUCTION` under `Q36_F2_2K1_A1_C7_A3_MULTIPLICITY_RIGIDITY.md`.

This records the exact secondary shell generated by the only nonclique multiplicity-three support still allowed algebraically in the c=7,A=3 terminal.

## 1. Equality data at the original q36 pivot

Let D be a support class of multiplicity3 in the one-edge equality form. Then

- `e_H(D)=1`;
- `m(D)=2`;
- `kappa(D)=0`;
- `e_F(x0,D)=0`;
- `e_F(Y,D)=0`;
- weighted overlap `O_D=4`.

Therefore

`lambda(D)=3*3+4=13`,

where lambda_v is the number of the seven low supports containing v.

For every v in D, because v lies in the 12-point remainder R it is target-anticomplete to the far pair, and the equalities above show it is also target-anticomplete to x0 and Y. Its only shell neighbours are its low owners. Hence

`g_v=lambda_v-1`.

Summing over D,

> `sum_D g_v=lambda(D)-3=10`.                              (1)

## 2. Repivot at an owner of D

Choose one of the three owners y of D and repivot at y.

The support defect is exactly2, so with common-S allowance3 the new charge is

> `q_y=35`.                                                 (2)

The repivot removes the common missing triple `F union {x0}`. It therefore removes the active decorated vertex x0 but retains all three inactive decorated vertices Y, whose total decoration is exactly3.

The inserted support D contributes decoration10 by (1). Thus

> `G_y=3+10=13`.                                           (3)

Every q35 shell has missing-edge count at least22 by inherited D14, while `q_y=z_y+G_y`. Equations (2)--(3) force

> `z_y=22`.                                                 (4)

Hence the secondary shell is D14-saturated.

## 3. Exact target graph of the new shell

The new 13-shell is

`A_y={p} union (C\{y}) union Y union D`.

The first ten vertices

`B={p} union (C\{y}) union Y`

form a target K10:

- p is adjacent to the old shell vertices;
- C is a target clique;
- Y is a target K3;
- every inactive y in Y is target-adjacent to every low owner.

The support D is target-anticomplete to `p union Y`.

Among the six remaining low owners in `C\{y}`:

- the other two owners from the multiplicity-three D-class are target-adjacent to all three D-vertices, contributing6 edges;
- the four remaining owner incidences account for the exact overlap O_D=4, and because O_D is saturated each such owner support meets D in exactly one point, contributing4 edges.

Therefore

> `e_F(D,B)=10`.                                           (5)

Together with the unique internal target edge of D, the new shell has exactly

`binom(10,2)+10+1=56`

target edges, hence `78-56=22` missing edges, agreeing with (4).

## 4. Exact regular missing-degree pattern

In the new shell:

- p is target-anticomplete to D, hence has missing degree3;
- the two remaining D-class owners see all of D, hence have missing degree0;
- each of the four other low owners sees exactly one D-vertex, hence has missing degree2;
- the three Y-vertices are decorated and miss all of D.

Thus the regular part of the secondary shell contains the exact pattern

> `d_M = 3,0,0,2,2,2,2`.                                  (6)

## 5. Interface

Every surviving c=7,A=3 case containing a multiplicity-three one-edge support generates this same q35 D14-equality shell. Further closure may therefore be carried out in the secondary q35 view rather than by repeating the original q36 support classification.
